decisions.subject: Heavyweight book
decisions.lean: A confirmed-defensive rotation that presses the firm's highest-signal ideas while holding ~30% cash as a deliberate hedge, not a shrug. The tape is a Goldilocks quad with expanding liquidity BUT a validated risk_off radar (bubble/blow-off unwind 60/100, bubble_leadership 96%, leaders distributing) — and Flagship just confirmed the migration by dumping SMH/XLK/MTUM/ANET into financials + defensives. I concentrate into the five names that actually carry positive confluence and, where possible, size_authority UP: JNJ (22%, research 84, +0.33, UP) as the low-beta anchor; CFG (15%) as the single best-confluence expression (+0.43) of the freshly-thrusting financials cluster; CHRW (12%, +0.33, UP) for confirmed logistics leadership; AME (11%) for trend-confirmed quality industrial; ACIW (10%) for uncorrelated payments-software growth. One name per cluster (CFG over XLF/USB; CHRW over EXPD; JNJ over XLV/CI). I dropped CI/SWK (out of universe) and refused to press APH despite a 74 research score because Flagship's own cycle lens vetoed it today (cycle_blocked) — I don't fight the firm's veto. The 30% cash is the froth hedge: if the blow-off unwind triggers, it's my dry powder and downside buffer.

decisions.subject: China book
decisions.lean: Today's decision corrects a structural flaw: the book was 61% cash against an FXI benchmark — a massive uncompensated passive short-equity bet left over from one tech-led risk-off night that has since passed. I redeploy dry powder to cut cash to ~22%, keeping a real defensive buffer because China-regime confidence is genuinely low (0.185) and the backdrop is growth-scare/risk-off with a USD headwind. The book leans into the one thing the desk actually confirms — HK Financials as the RS leader (~92.9th pctile), geared to the building PBoC easing impulse and the pending Q3→Q2 regime shift toward recovery: China Life (2628.HK), Ping An (2318.HK), China Construction Bank (0939.HK) and ICBC (1398.HK) form a ~36% financials sleeve. I add the FXI-core names I was glaringly missing to kill tracking error — Alibaba (9988.HK) for tech breadth and China Mobile (0941.HK) as high-dividend, low-beta risk-off ballast — while Tencent (0700.HK) is bumped back to a 12% quality-tech anchor. Defensive ballast is rounded out by my innovative-drugs winner CSPC (1093.HK) and utility Power Assets (0006.HK). I exited Bank of China (3988.HK), my worst and lowest-conviction holding, consolidating SOE-bank quality into CCB. Net: a diversified, FXI-aware book tilted to confirmed financials leadership with measured tech participation and ~22% dry powder.
decisions.thesis: Fully exited Bank of China (3988.HK) — my worst-performing, lowest-conviction holding — consolidating the SOE-bank dividend sleeve into the higher-quality China Construction Bank (0939.HK). Trimmed China Life (2628.HK) slightly (~14.1%→13%) to make room for a broader financials sleeve. Deployed roughly 39% of NAV out of cash (61%→~22%) into FXI-core financials, telecom and tech to reduce a large passive benchmark underweight.
